bug_semantics: The authenticated report.list tRPC procedure accepted two independent tenant selectors. Middleware authorized the caller only against the supplied projectId, while the handler passed the independently supplied dashboardId to getReportsByDashboardId(), whose database predicate was only { dashboardId }. A caller could therefore submit an owned projectId to pass middleware and another organization's dashboardId to enumerate that dashboard's reports.
flaw_origin: PR #211 member commit 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec first added packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts:11-20, including report.list and the unscoped return getReportsByDashboardId(dashboardId). The PR was later squash-landed as 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d; the reconstructed member chain proves 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec, not the squash aggregate, is the smallest BIC.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object names human author and committer Carl-Gerhard Lindesvärd <lindesvard@gmail.com>, has message exactly "wip", and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: First-party advisory: https://github.com/Openpanel-dev/openpanel/security/advisories/GHSA-3q95-vc6f-vc9v and its structured API record https://api.github.com/repos/Openpanel-dev/openpanel/security-advisories/GHSA-3q95-vc6f-vc9v describe the cross-organization report enumeration, identify packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts and packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts, give affected version 2.2.0 and patched version 2.3.0, and report live validation at e8a0602cda5a4d4b463f11d298a1b078c446bf33.

Squash decomposition: https://api.github.com/repos/Openpanel-dev/openpanel/pulls/211/commits?per_page=100 exposes the 44-member linear PR chain from 68d194e8c6a1dd52913fb5fed4c01aa2fc27d823 through 330321405d2ba207cb1672d1d38a4f0cdac85ad8. git -S over that chain finds the first additions of both `list: protectedProcedure` and `return getReportsByDashboardId(dashboardId);` in 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec (https://github.com/Openpanel-dev/openpanel/commit/3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec). The final member tree bd678581f1cc78a42ff07619c4bd7051c7c69cbb exactly equals squash commit 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d's tree (https://github.com/Openpanel-dev/openpanel/commit/81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d).

Direct-parent verification: `git diff 68d194e8c6a1dd52913fb5fed4c01aa2fc27d823 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec -- packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts` adds the vulnerable import and complete report.list block at lines 11-20. `git show 68d194e8c6a1dd52913fb5fed4c01aa2fc27d823:packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts` contains reportRouter starting directly with create, and `git grep` in that parent finds none of `list: protectedProcedure`, `getReportsByDashboardId`, or the vulnerable return. Parent URL: https://github.com/Openpanel-dev/openpanel/commit/68d194e8c6a1dd52913fb5fed4c01aa2fc27d823.

Attack-path source evidence at the BIC: packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts:90-108 authorizes only rawInput.projectId and lines 147-151 attach that middleware to protectedProcedure; packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts:11-20 then ignores projectId and queries by dashboardId; packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:74-81 uses only `where: { dashboardId }`. The project-scoped packages/db/src/services/dashboard.service.ts:12-27 helper already accepted `(id, projectId)`, but the new route did not call it.

Direct fix: https://github.com/Openpanel-dev/openpanel/commit/0a51b6805eed0b3da8376175acd5fa3d26819cb6 (parent a45bdb0f9372d8d4ef61f313b41142b63a2140e2) changes packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts so report.list calls `getDashboardById(dashboardId, projectId)`, throws TRPCNotFoundError when the pair does not resolve, and only then calls getReportsByDashboardId. `git show` of the direct parent still has the vulnerable lines at report.ts:11-20, proving this commit is the direct mechanism fix.

Version-boundary cross-check: the first-party advisory API explicitly records `vulnerable_version_range: "2.2.0"` and `patched_versions: "2.3.0"`. Docker Hub metadata at https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/lindesvard/openpanel-api/tags?page_size=100 confirms distinct published tags: 2.2.0 index digest sha256:1f77bc9fec0755b4bafd9ee7789364bbf6ec9909b7f86e6dc3b0c1dbd71168cf (image created 2026-02-06T20:29:55Z) and 2.3.0 digest sha256:cee4855cd715a7248c5c49090fe93a28ffc505541de20cb238d8884a6bcb9223 (created 2026-08-18T21:22:28Z). The time-aligned main snapshot ed8b5c667e6dd7f7b960c60ea5be9ce8c11ad8e1 for 2.2.0 contains the vulnerable report.ts:11-20, while 373be136190aa73debd4508fa4ac05619ce04a53 for 2.3.0 contains the scoped check at lines 23-28. Squash carrier 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d is an ancestor of both snapshots; fix 0a51b6805eed0b3da8376175acd5fa3d26819cb6 is not an ancestor of the 2.2.0 snapshot and is an ancestor of the 2.3.0 snapshot.

BIC-only AI check: `git cat-file -p 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec` gives parent 68d194e8c6a1dd52913fb5fed4c01aa2fc27d823, human author/committer Carl-Gerhard Lindesvärd <lindesvard@gmail.com>, and body `wip`; there is no AI attribution trailer or bot identity.
reasoning: The vulnerability is caused by an authorization-key mismatch, not by the database helper alone: getReportsByDashboardId had existed since 2024, but no vulnerable report.list exposure existed in the decomposed parent's router. PR #211 member 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec first composed the exploitable path by accepting projectId for middleware authorization while reading reports solely through caller-controlled dashboardId. Its direct parent lacks that route and both vulnerable symbols. The later one-parent mainline commit 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d is only a squash carrier because the public PR member chain is reconstructable and its final tree equals the squash tree. The flaw remained in the advisory's tested e8a0602cda5a4d4b463f11d298a1b078c446bf33 baseline and affected 2.2.0. Commit 0a51b6805eed0b3da8376175acd5fa3d26819cb6 directly repaired the route by resolving dashboardId together with projectId before the unscoped report lookup, and it is present before the 2.3.0 fixed boundary. Finally, the exact smallest BIC commit object has only a human author/committer and no AI marker, so BIC-only attribution requires NOT_AI.
